chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan and Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man upon whom multiple penalties had gathered, including killing, he said: Begin with the penalties that are less than killing, then he is killed afterwards.
ai.seo_question: What is the order of executing multiple hudud penalties when one is death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the jurisprudential principle of 'Taqdim al-Aqall' (prioritizing the lesser) when multiple hudud penalties converge on a single individual. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that distinct penalties are executed sequentially to ensure justice, rather than being merged or cancelled, with the death penalty serving as the final, definitive conclusion to the judicial process.
